# Installing Claude Code

Before we can start building, we need to install Claude Code. This is straightforward---just one command in the Terminal.

## Step 1: Install Claude Code

Open Terminal and paste this command:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
```

:::{.callout-note}
For the latest installation instructions, visit the [Claude Code documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart).
:::

Press Enter. The installer will download and set up Claude Code automatically. This might take a minute or two.

When it's done, verify the installation worked:

```bash
claude --version
```

You should see a version number.

## Step 2: First Launch

Navigate to your project folder (the one we created in the previous chapter):

```bash
cd ~/Projects/my-app
```

Now launch Claude Code:

```bash
claude
```

The first time you run Claude Code, it will ask you to authenticate. This connects Claude Code to your Anthropic account.

:::{.callout-note}
## Choosing a Plan
When you create your Anthropic account, you'll choose a subscription tier. Each tier has rate limits---caps on how much you can use Claude Code in a given time window.

**Free** works for light exploration, but you'll likely hit limits quickly during active development.

**Pro ($20/month)** is enough for most founders building their first project. You get roughly 45 messages every 5 hours before limits kick in.

**Max plans** ($100-200/month) offer more capacity for heavier usage or larger projects.

If you hit a rate limit, Claude Code will pause until the window resets (every 5 hours). Your work isn't lost---you just wait or upgrade.

For current pricing details, visit [claude.ai/pricing](https://claude.ai/pricing).
:::

Follow the prompts:

1. Claude Code will open a browser window (or give you a URL to open)
2. Log in to your Anthropic account (or create one if you don't have one)
3. Authorize Claude Code to access your account
4. Return to the Terminal

Once authenticated, you'll see Claude Code's interface---a prompt where you can type messages and get responses.

## Step 3: Verify Everything Works

Let's make sure everything is set up correctly.

:::{.callout-tip}
## Example Prompt
"Help me verify that everything is installed correctly. Check that I have git available."
:::

Claude Code will run some checks and let you know if anything is missing. If something isn't working, it will suggest how to fix it.

## Understanding the Interface

When Claude Code is running, you'll see a prompt that looks something like:

```
>
```

Type your message and press Enter. Claude Code will respond, potentially running commands or creating files as needed.

Some useful things to know:

- Type `/help` to see available commands
- Type `/exit` or press `Ctrl+C` (or `Ctrl+D`) to quit Claude Code
- Press `Esc` to cancel Claude Code mid-response if it's going in the wrong direction
- Claude Code remembers the context of your conversation within a session
- Use `/resume` to continue a previous session where you left off

## If Something Went Wrong

Installation issues are common and usually fixable. Here are some things to try:

**The curl command failed:**
If you have Homebrew installed, you can try this alternative:

```bash
brew install --cask claude-code
```

If you don't have Homebrew, visit [brew.sh](https://brew.sh) to install it first, then run the command above.

**"Command not found" after installation:**
Close Terminal completely and open a new window. Sometimes Terminal needs to restart to recognize new commands.

**Authentication problems:**
Make sure you have an active internet connection and that you've created an Anthropic account at [anthropic.com](https://anthropic.com).

:::{.callout-tip}
## Example Prompt
"I got this error when trying to install: [paste the error]. What should I do?"
:::

When in doubt, ask Claude Code. Even if it's not fully installed yet, you can use Claude (the web version at claude.ai) to troubleshoot installation issues.

## Next Steps

With Claude Code installed and working, you're ready to start building. But first, let's make sure you understand the landscape---what a "tech stack" is and what the pieces of a modern application look like.
